channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Students work to save a plant found only near their campus [6/10]
item.description: Santa Clara University scientists are protecting the Santa Clara Valley liveforever, a rare succulent threatened by poaching. (Goodness 6/10: Local conservation effort protecting a very rare plant.)

item.title: Antarctic blue whale population grows about tenfold since whaling ended [8/10]
item.description: Antarctic blue whales rose from 418 individuals in 1973 to roughly 4,018, growing about 4.5% a year after commercial whaling stopped. (Goodness 8/10: Clear recovery of a once-nearly-extinct species, though numbers remain small.)

item.title: Two women turn burnt crop straw into a business [7/10]
item.description: Founders from Haryana and Rajasthan started SSAR Biomass Green, turning farm straw that is often burned into useful products. (Goodness 7/10: Reduces burning and pollution while creating income.)

item.title: India wins 10th SAFF football title with a second-string squad [6/10]
item.description: India beat Pakistan to claim its tenth SAFF Championship title without its star players. (Goodness 6/10: Sporting success and community pride.)

item.title: Rescued olive ridley sea turtle hatchlings released into the Pacific [6/10]
item.description: Olive ridley hatchlings rescued ahead of a California storm were released into the Pacific, described as the first such release on the US West Coast. (Goodness 6/10: A small but hopeful rescue of a threatened species.)

item.title: Earthshot Prize winners honoured in Mumbai [6/10]
item.description: Prince William presented five Earthshot Prize winners with one million pounds each for environmental solutions at a ceremony in Mumbai. (Goodness 6/10: Funding boosts proven environmental projects.)

item.title: Fela Kuti becomes first African inducted into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame [7/10]
item.description: The Nigerian Afrobeat pioneer has been inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the first African artist to receive the honour. (Goodness 7/10: A landmark recognition for African music.)

item.title: Scimitar-horned oryx returns to Chad [8/10]
item.description: A reintroduction programme led by Sahara Conservation has rebuilt a wild population of the scimitar-horned oryx in Chad. (Goodness 8/10: Successful return of a species once extinct in the wild.)

item.title: Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion in shares ahead of Thanksgiving [7/10]
item.description: Warren Buffett converted Berkshire Hathaway shares into a $5.5 billion gift for charitable foundations, saying kindness is important. (Goodness 7/10: Large donation helping many causes.)

item.title: New York's largest electric school bus fleet serves a South Bronx neighborhood [7/10]
item.description: The largest electric school bus fleet in New York State now runs in a South Bronx neighborhood with high childhood asthma rates, cutting exposure to diesel exhaust. (Goodness 7/10: Cleaner air for children in a high-asthma area.)

item.title: Rewari revives 10 ponds to store water as groundwater falls [7/10]
item.description: TERI and Nokia India are restoring 10 village ponds in Haryana's Rewari district over 24 months, aiming to store 120 million litres of water. (Goodness 7/10: Practical local water security, though results are still to come.)

item.title: Indian startup turns crop stubble into biochar [7/10]
item.description: Takachar, an Earthshot Awards winner, uses portable equipment to convert crop stubble into biochar, offering farmers an alternative to burning. (Goodness 7/10: Could cut field-burning smoke, if it scales.)

item.title: African artists take four of five global album spots in 2027 Grammy nominations [6/10]
item.description: African musicians received four of the five nominations in the Grammy global music album category. (Goodness 6/10: Wider recognition of African music.)

item.title: Proposed marine protected area could safeguard whale sharks in Indonesia [6/10]
item.description: Plans for a marine protected area in Indonesia's Saleh Bay would cover important habitat for whale sharks. (Goodness 6/10: Still a plan, not yet in force.)

item.title: Somerset volunteers take on the perspectives of local wildlife [6/10]
item.description: Volunteers in the River Tone catchment in Somerset took on the viewpoints of animals such as kestrels to rethink how the landscape is managed. (Goodness 6/10: A creative community approach to nature recovery.)

item.title: AIIMS Delhi performs open foetal surgery at 25 weeks [7/10]
item.description: Surgeons at AIIMS Delhi repaired myelomeningocele, a spinal defect, in a baby before birth at 25 weeks of pregnancy. (Goodness 7/10: A medical milestone, though for a small number of patients.)

item.title: Japanese town uses rice paddies to hold floodwater [7/10]
item.description: Osaki has installed more than 5,000 small earthen dams in surrounding rice paddies so the fields can hold floodwater and reduce flooding. (Goodness 7/10: Low-cost climate adaptation using existing farmland.)

item.title: Forever chemicals fall in English rivers and fish [7/10]
item.description: Two internationally restricted PFAS chemicals have dropped about 30% in English river water and 49% in fish, according to a BBC report. (Goodness 7/10: Restrictions are visibly working, though the chemicals persist.)

item.title: Maharashtra village runs without electricity bills [7/10]
item.description: A video report looks at Shelkewadi, a Maharashtra village that has cut its electricity bills and supplies cooking gas through local energy projects. (Goodness 7/10: A community model that others could copy.)

item.title: Tokyo trials robotic street bins in tourist areas [6/10]
item.description: Tokyo is using solar-powered compactors and robots to haul rubbish away from busy tourist districts while keeping its tradition of tidy streets. (Goodness 6/10: A practical urban fix, limited to one city.)

item.title: 17-year-old builds AI tool to help blind people read documents [6/10]
item.description: Yash Bhatnagar, 17, created Visionably, an AI tool that helps blind people read bank statements and textbooks. (Goodness 6/10: Useful accessibility tech from a young creator, still early stage.)

item.title: Hera spacecraft images the crater-covered side of NASA-impacted asteroid [6/10]
item.description: ESA's Hera mission has imaged the asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's 2022 impact, revealing a surprising cratered surface. (Goodness 6/10: Useful planetary defence knowledge.)

item.title: A firefly species not seen since 1983 is found again in the US [7/10]
item.description: The similar firefly, last documented in 1983, was recorded in Virginia and Delaware in spring 2026. (Goodness 7/10: A rediscovery that offers hope for overlooked insects.)

item.title: AIIMS Delhi performs India's first open foetal repair [7/10]
item.description: Doctors at AIIMS Delhi report India's first open foetal surgery repair, a procedure years in the making. (Goodness 7/10: A medical first that could help future families, though currently for few patients.)

item.title: Climbers carry orphaned monk seal pup up a cliff [6/10]
item.description: Hikers in Greece found an orphaned seal pup on a beach below a cliff and carried it back up to safety. (Goodness 6/10: A small rescue for an endangered animal.)

item.title: Band that voiced Sudan's revolution records together again in Cairo [6/10]
item.description: Musician Mohamed al-Mustafa is recording in Cairo with his band, whose members were scattered across countries by the war in Sudan. (Goodness 6/10: A cultural comeback amid ongoing conflict.)

item.title: Charity donates bicycles to people seeking asylum in the UK [6/10]
item.description: The Bike Project gives bicycles to asylum seekers in the UK, helping with transport poverty and daily life. (Goodness 6/10: Helps many people directly, on a modest scale.)

item.title: Barbershop blood-pressure screenings aim to improve Black men's health [7/10]
item.description: The CLIP program brought blood-pressure screenings into 22 Black-owned barbershops, using community trust to reach men who often avoid clinics. (Goodness 7/10: Practical health outreach for an underserved group.)

item.title: Rare flat-headed cat recorded in Sarawak mangrove [6/10]
item.description: A camera-trap survey in a Sarawak mangrove recorded the endangered flat-headed cat and showed it prefers elevated palms. (Goodness 6/10: New knowledge that can guide protection of a rare species.)

item.title: Indian startup makes leather alternative from tomato waste [6/10]
item.description: The Bio Company turns discarded tomatoes into a material that can replace animal leather. (Goodness 6/10: An early-stage startup, but it reuses waste and avoids animal leather.)

item.title: Wrist device cut Tourette's tics by a quarter in UK trial [6/10]
item.description: A trial with 121 people found that the Neupulse prototype wrist device reduced tic frequency by about 25 percent. (Goodness 6/10: A modest, drug-free benefit from a prototype in a small trial.)

item.title: First bone marrow transplant for a non-cancerous disease reported [7/10]
item.description: Franciscan Health reports treating aplastic anemia with marrow from a deceased donor, a world first for a non-malignant disease. (Goodness 7/10: A promising first that may widen donor options, though one reported case.)

item.title: San Francisco receives $100 million gift for public parks [7/10]
item.description: Airbnb co-founder Brian Chesky announced a $100 million donation to the city's parks, the largest single-donor gift San Francisco has received. (Goodness 7/10: A large philanthropic gift will improve shared green space.)

item.title: Osteoporosis drug prevented spinal degeneration in a study [6/10]
item.description: Researchers linked a genetic factor to spinal degeneration and showed that an existing osteoporosis drug prevented the damage in the experiments. (Goodness 6/10: Early research, but it points to repurposing an approved drug.)

item.title: Pune residents map riverside trees to protect urban greenery [6/10]
item.description: Volunteers use phone apps and measuring tapes to document trees along Pune's rivers, building evidence to support conservation. (Goodness 6/10: Citizen-led data can strengthen the case for protecting city trees.)

item.title: Maharashtra village cuts electricity bills using biogas and solar [7/10]
item.description: Shelkewadi in Kolhapur district relies on biogas, solar power and related systems to avoid electricity costs. (Goodness 7/10: A community-scale clean energy example others could copy.)

item.title: Kenyan conservationist Raabia Hawa wins 2026 Tusk Award [7/10]
item.description: Raabia Hawa, founder of the Ulinzi Africa Foundation, is honoured for defending Kenya's ecosystems despite being targeted by al-Shabaab. (Goodness 7/10: Recognition for a conservation leader, which can support her work.)

item.title: Euclid telescope finds 31 early quasars, two of them record-setting [6/10]
item.description: ESA's Euclid space telescope identified 31 quasars from the early universe, including two that set new records. (Goodness 6/10: A scientific advance with no direct everyday benefit.)

item.title: Two remote Pacific atolls declared sanctuaries [7/10]
item.description: Two of the Pacific coral atolls that scientists consider among the last wild ecosystems untouched by humans have been declared new sanctuaries. (Goodness 7/10: Protecting nearly pristine reefs is a lasting gain for marine life.)

item.title: Consistent daily routine linked to less pain and depression in older adults [6/10]
item.description: University of Missouri researchers found that older adults with regular daily schedules reported less pain and fewer depressive symptoms. (Goodness 6/10: Simple habit with possible benefit, though the study shows a link, not proof.)

item.title: Stanford team finds brain signals that may predict Alzheimer's early [6/10]
item.description: Stanford researchers found brain activity patterns that may flag Alzheimer's risk years before symptoms appear, earlier than current tools. (Goodness 6/10: Promising for early detection, but still early research.)

item.title: Zimbabwe village keeps elephants off crops without harming them [6/10]
item.description: Villagers combine non-lethal measures, such as chili-laced balls and burning dung, to protect their fields from elephants. (Goodness 6/10: A low-cost, harmless way to reduce human-wildlife conflict in one village.)

item.title: South African court blocks planned coal power plants [7/10]
item.description: South Africa's Supreme Court of Appeal upheld a ruling striking down plans for 1,500 MW of new coal-fired power capacity. (Goodness 7/10: Avoids new coal emissions, though the project could return in other forms.)

item.title: Five ways to cut emissions from buildings [6/10]
item.description: Buildings produce about 27 percent of global emissions, and the article outlines five approaches that lower their carbon footprint. (Goodness 6/10: Useful solutions for a large source of emissions.)

item.title: Fruit bats help restore Brazil's Atlantic Forest [6/10]
item.description: Researchers are studying how fruit-eating bats spread seeds, making them useful partners in regrowing the damaged forest. (Goodness 6/10: Natural seed dispersal can speed up forest recovery, but the work is at research stage.)

item.title: Nigeria reports no Ebola spread after imported case [6/10]
item.description: Nigeria has recorded no new Ebola cases since a woman arriving from Uganda tested positive last month, and her contacts finished 21 days of monitoring uninfected. (Goodness 6/10: Containment worked in Nigeria, while the wider outbreak continues.)

item.title: Teen helps turn Bengaluru school storeroom into 2,000-book library [6/10]
item.description: Seventeen-year-old Asavari Agrawal helped convert a school storage room into a library of 2,000 books. (Goodness 6/10: A local project that widens access to books.)

item.title: Infant in Dubai becomes seizure-free after experimental drug [6/10]
item.description: A baby in Dubai who had a seizure about every 13 minutes since birth stopped having seizures after receiving an experimental drug. Follow-up so far covers only weeks. (Goodness 6/10: Dramatic result for one child, but the treatment is experimental and the follow-up is short.)

item.title: Swiss hospital discharges Ebola patient after treatment [6/10]
item.description: A Swiss woman infected with the Ebola strain linked to the DR Congo outbreak was discharged after successful treatment. (Goodness 6/10: A good outcome for one patient amid a wider outbreak.)

item.title: Bengaluru startup converts office air conditioners into air purifiers [6/10]
item.description: Clairco, a Bengaluru startup, retrofits office air conditioners to purify air. The company says its technology benefits around 1.5 million people. (Goodness 6/10: Useful local innovation; the reach figure is the company's own claim.)

item.title: US voters approve $27 billion in transit measures [7/10]
item.description: Voters approved 22 of 27 transit ballot measures on November 3, worth about $27.4 billion for repairs and expansion of transit systems. (Goodness 7/10: Broad funding for public transport, though delivery depends on officials.)

item.title: Maui explores regenerative tourism after the Lahaina fires [6/10]
item.description: Residents and businesses on Maui are testing tourism models meant to restore communities and nature, following the 2023 wildfires that destroyed much of Lahaina. (Goodness 6/10: A recovery-focused approach, though still experimental.)

item.title: Two engineers turn waste from 46 lakh people into compost [7/10]
item.description: Two engineers run waste collection for about 4.6 million people and convert the waste into compost. (Goodness 7/10: Large-scale waste reuse that reduces landfill.)

item.title: Tagged spoon-billed sandpiper travels from Russia to Bengal coast [6/10]
item.description: A critically endangered spoon-billed sandpiper tagged in Russia in July 2025 has been tracked to the coast of Bengal. (Goodness 6/10: Tracking data helps protect a species close to extinction.)

item.title: Dehradun founders build pocket-sized ECG device [6/10]
item.description: Sunfox Technologies built Spandan, a smartphone-connected ECG device that gives a heart reading in about two minutes, aimed at rural India. (Goodness 6/10: Low-cost diagnostics can widen access to heart checks.)

item.title: Wastewater plant in New Jersey installs microplastics-capturing system [6/10]
item.description: A treatment plant in Atlantic City has installed a system designed by former Princeton students that traps microplastics before they reach the ocean, mimicking wetland plants. (Goodness 6/10: Promising pilot-style technology at a single plant so far.)

item.title: China starts world's largest liquid-air energy storage plant [7/10]
item.description: A demonstration plant in western China now stores renewable electricity by liquefying air, then releasing it to drive a turbine when power is needed. (Goodness 7/10: A large demonstration of cheap grid storage, though still a demonstration plant.)

item.title: Taiwan tea growers turn to natural cultivation as climate shifts [6/10]
item.description: Alishan oolong growers are moving away from chemical inputs toward natural and wild cultivation to adapt to climate change. (Goodness 6/10: A community adapting in a way that benefits the land.)

item.title: Assam restricts drones near Amur falcon roosts [6/10]
item.description: Assam's Forest Department restricted unauthorised drone operations near Amur falcon roosts to keep the birds' migration undisturbed. (Goodness 6/10: A practical protection for migratory birds.)

item.title: Los Angeles bans new oil drilling and phases out existing wells [8/10]
item.description: The city council banned new oil drilling and will phase out existing operations within city limits over 20 years, after a decade of pressure from nearby residents. (Goodness 8/10: Meaningful health and climate gain for neighbourhoods near wells, with a long phase-out.)
